claim: Mitochondria are critical for the survival of apicomplexans.

evidence: Supported by citations to Doggett et al., 2012; Phillips et al., 2008; Srivastava et al., 1999

claim: 51% of the T. gondii mitochondrial proteome lacks orthologs in animals.

claim: Of the T. gondii mitochondrial proteins lacking orthologs in animals, 56% had orthologs in other apicomplexans and/or chromerids.

claim: 161 proteins in the T. gondii mitochondrial proteome have homologs in yeast.

claim: Of the 161 T. gondii mitochondrial proteins with yeast homologs, 103 were predicted to localize to the yeast mitochondrion.

claim: 35% of proteins from the mitochondrial proteome were critical for parasite growth.

claim: Of the proteins conserved between T. gondii and apicomplexans/chromerids, over 80% were important or critical for parasite growth.

claim: Over 70% of proteins collectively found in apicomplexans, chromerids and animals were important or critical for parasite growth.

claim: TgApiCox25 has a predicted molecular mass of 25 kDa.

claim: TgApiCox25 localizes to the mitochondrion.

claim: TgApiCox25-HA protein is substantially depleted 2 days after ATc addition in rTgApiCox25 parasites.

claim: TgApiCox25-HA protein is barely detectable after 3 days in ATc in rTgApiCox25 parasites.

claim: Growth of rTgApiCox25 parasites is severely impaired in the presence of ATc.

claim: rTgApiCox25 parasites grew better in the absence of ATc than WT parasites.

claim: Growth of TgApiCox25 parasites for 2 or 3 days in ATc resulted in a slight increase in ECAR.

claim: Parasites remained metabolically active upon TgApiCox25 knockdown.

claim: Knockdown of TgApiCox25 did not lead to gross morphological defects in mitochondria.

claim: rTgApiCox25 parasites treated for 3 days on ATc have equivalent viability to rTgApiCox25 not grown on ATc.

evidence: Supported by plaque assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B

claim: TgApiCox25 has an important, specific role in oxidative phosphorylation in T. gondii parasites.

claim: TgApiCox25 is a component of a ~ 600 kDa protein complex in the parasite mitochondrion.

claim: 12 proteins, including TgApiCox25, were enriched in the TgApiCox25-HA immunoprecipitation compared to the TgTom40-HA immunoprecipitation.

claim: Three of the 12 proteins enriched in TgApiCox25-HA immunoprecipitation are annotated as being canonical components of cytochrome c oxidase (COX).

claim: 7 of the remaining 8 TgApiCox25-associated proteins have homologs in other apicomplexans as well as in chromerids.

claim: TgApiCox16 (TGGT1_265370) is restricted to T. gondii.

claim: All of the proteins detected in the TgApiCox25 complex were identified in the mitochondrial proteome.

claim: All proteins in the TgApiCox25 complex except TgApiCox16 are predicted to be important for growth of the tachyzoite stage of T. gondii.

claim: The T. gondii mitochondrial proteome identified approximately 400 putative mitochondrial proteins.

evidence: Describes the results of the study

claim: The T. gondii mitochondrial proteome is slightly lower than the 495 proteins identified in the mtAPEX-derived proteome of mammalian cells.
source: This number is slightly lower than the 495 proteins identified in the mtAPEX-derived proteome of mammalian cells (Rhee et al., 2013), and is less than the 750 – 900 proteins identified in yeast studies using highly purified mitochondria (Morgenstern et al., 2017; Sickmann et al., 2003).

claim: The 208 proteins found in the mtBirA* proteome alone are considered 'possible' mitochondrial proteins.

claim: This study is the first time the APEX and BirA* restricted biotinylation approaches have been directly compared in organellar proteomic approaches.

evidence: Authors' assessment of novelty

claim: A large number of proteins in the T. gondii mitochondrion have homologs in P. falciparum.

claim: This is consistent with the presence of similar mitochondrial processes and biochemical pathways in T. gondii and P. falciparum.

claim: The lower value of homologs in C. parvum is consistent with the reduced function of the mitosome of this organism.

claim: Several 'derived' features of apicomplexan mitochondria were already present in the free-living, autotrophic common ancestor of myzozoans.

claim: Much of the mitochondrial biology in T. gondii was present in the free-living ancestor that they share with chromerids.

claim: The T. gondii COX complex is larger than the equivalent complex in yeast (200 kDa), mammals (200 kDa) and plants (220/300 kDa).
